issues.title: Phase 1 does not explicitly enumerate the 6 command files to scaffold
issues.details: The classification table identifies 6 nodes needing *-codex command variants (implement-tasks, pr-review-scope, code-review-agent, error-handling-agent, docs-impact-agent, implement-review-fixes), but Phase 1 only says 'create the required *-codex.md command files' without listing them. Derivable from the table, but the table and Phase 1 could drift independently.
issues.suggested_fix: Add an explicit file list to Phase 1 referencing the classification table rows, or add a cross-reference note.

issues.title: Phase 3 validator rule does not specify explicit provider: <other> on a Codex workflow node
issues.details: Phase 3 specifies catching inference-based leaks (node model string infers non-Codex provider). It does not state whether a node with explicit provider: claude inside a provider: codex workflow should also be an error. This may be intentional (explicit cross-provider nodes could be valid), but the plan doesn't say.
issues.suggested_fix: Add one sentence clarifying whether explicit cross-provider node overrides are in-scope or intentionally excluded from this rule.

issues.title: model: inherit edge case is not called out
issues.details: registry.ts:117 maps 'inherit' to Claude and registry.ts:129 excludes it from Codex. inferProviderFromModel('inherit', 'codex') returns 'claude', which the proposed validator rule would catch. But 'inherit' is a non-obvious model value that the plan doesn't mention. If a future command accidentally uses model: inherit, the validator would correctly reject it — but implementers should know this edge case exists.
issues.suggested_fix: Add 'inherit' to the Phase 3 test cases in validator.test.ts alongside claude-opus-4-6 as a documented edge case.

recommended_fixes: Add explicit file list to Phase 1 matching the 6 *-codex rows in the classification table
Clarify Phase 3 scope: does the validator rule apply only to inference-based leaks, or also to explicit cross-provider node overrides?
Add model: inherit as a documented edge case in Phase 3 test coverage
review.best_case: The plan delivers a clean Codex-native workflow that statically validates, catches provider escape at validation time (not just runtime), and ships without touching the Claude baseline. The classification table is accurate, the phasing is correct, and the validator extension fills a real gap that protects all future Codex workflows — not just this one.
strongest_objections: The plan relies on grep-based audits (Phase 2) as the primary evidence for provider-neutral classification, which is fragile against false negatives if Claude assumptions are expressed in natural language rather than keywords — but this is acknowledged by the 're-confirm every provider-neutral command' instruction

Phase 3 extends the validator for a specific scenario (model-inferred provider ≠ workflow provider) without specifying whether the broader case (explicit cross-provider overrides) is intentionally in or out of scope

The plan creates 6 new command files as 'mechanical copies with obvious Claude-provider wording removed' which risks subtle prompt quality issues that only surface at runtime — but Phase 5 smoke run is designed to catch exactly this
hidden_assumptions: Claude's isModelCompatible iterates first in getRegisteredProviders() — if registration order changes, inferProviderFromModel could return different results
The plan assumes Codex provider capabilities won't gain MCP/hooks/skills support before implementation — if they do, some classification decisions change

'Mechanical copies with wording removed' assumes the command prompts are mostly provider-neutral already — if the prompt logic deeply depends on Claude-specific behavior (tool use patterns, output formatting), the copies may need more than wording changes
review.what_would_change_my_mind: If reading the actual command files for the 6 planned *-codex variants revealed that their prompts deeply depend on Claude-specific tool behaviors (TodoWrite, multi-turn tool chaining, specific output parsing) rather than just containing Claude-branded wording, the mechanical-copy approach in Phase 1 would be insufficient and the phasing would need restructuring. A single read of archon-implement-tasks.md (already done, lines 1-60) suggests the prompts are mostly procedural, which supports the plan's approach.
next_checks: Read the remaining 5 command files (pr-review-scope, code-review-agent, error-handling-agent, docs-impact-agent, implement-review-fixes) to verify the classification table before implementation
Confirm that getRegisteredProviders() iteration order is deterministic (Map insertion order in JS) so inferProviderFromModel behaves predictably
